items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: when I wrote 'Down Hearted Blues'... I hummed this thing to her... she said, oh, maybe we can make a record of that.

ctx.x: But now Lovie Austin used to dress in leopard skin?

She drove that Stutz. She drove that Stutz Bearcat, yeah. She wasn't so smartly dressed. Her car was smart. But she -- her clothes didn't have the fashion that Lil's had. Uh-uh, she didn't have the fashion. But she had that Stutz car, boy. She could drive it like she bought an oil field, she'd go so fast, you know. Several times I think she asked me to ride when I had some place to go; I didn't want to get in that car with Lovie, because Lovie was going too fast. I wanted to live a little longer, you know.

items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: I had moved over to 32nd and Dearborn, to a lady named Miss Bern... instead of staying at Mrs. Love's... There was a lady washing. Her name was Miss Love... So I said, 'Lady, do you know a girl around here by the name of Ellen Winston?'... And she said yes.

ctx.x: No. So I started singing the blues, and the people used to come to hear me singing the blues, and especially Downhearted Blues. And the girl, Love Austin, heard me. She came and heard me. She was playing at the old
Monogram, one of the little joints there, theater, you know, little funny theater.
